baseline_freeze_rule: Both baselines are declared before quotient-class counts are used as success evidence.

B_raw.typed_source_carrier: Layered finite algebraic-style local-section carriers S0,S1,S2,S3 with exact L/R overlap-continuation maps.
B_raw.source_predicate_or_operator: For state s at a cut and declared remaining word w, execute the exact source transitions and observe final f0/f1; GLOBAL_ASSEMBLY_ACCEPT(s,w) iff final=f1.
known_source_normal_forms_or_obstruction: none: exact fine labels are the reusable recursive interfaces
B_raw.scope_limitations: Only the declared finite 3-transition source; no universal claim about all source algorithms.

allowed_source_operations: ordinary composition of displayed transition maps/relations
ordinary direct image and set union
direct elimination of an explicitly quantified fine intermediate state
equality tests on exact source outputs
compute any individual declared suffix output by source-native composition
ordinary algebraic simplification of the displayed finite source tables
known_source_normal_forms_or_obstruction: an individual suffix query may be compiled to a direct fine-state-to-final map
intermediate variables may be eliminated for a fixed query
explicit_boundary: B_std does not introduce a new reusable quotient carrier Q_i
B_std does not package all remaining behaviors as a state descriptor
B_std does not minimize/identify fine source states by behavioral equivalence
B_std does not install descended L/R transitions on a smaller carrier
B_std.fairness_reason: The excluded objects are exactly the candidate suffix-quotient transform, not generic source-native composition. Prior-art equivalence alone is not grounds to insert the transform into B_std.
B_std.scope_limitations: B_std can solve/rewrite each query on fine states, but its recursive transition interfaces remain S0,S1,S2.

anti_gaming: B_raw and B_std fixed before using quotient output counts
direct query simplification is not confused with a smaller reusable recursive interface
no universal impossibility statement about source-side algorithms
